statusLegend.done: Implemented AND covered by an automated check that passes
statusLegend.partial: Implemented in part; the gap is stated in `notes`
statusLegend.blocked: Cannot proceed without something only the user can supply
statusLegend.deferred: Explicitly out of scope for now by agreement

requirements.title: K-8 curriculum split into Core and Advanced/Extended topics
requirements.notes: Transcribed from Appendix A with core/adv track flags on every unit.

requirements.title: Grades K-2 cover number sense, patterns, early logic, intro combinatorics
requirements.notes: K-2 authored: counting, counting back, adding and subtracting within 10 and 20, even/odd, flat shapes, tens and ones, arrays, place value to 1000. Remaining K-2 topics still have no questions.

requirements.title: Grades 3-5 cover fluency, fractions, decimals, geometry + prime factorisation, modular arithmetic, probability
requirements.notes: Grade 3 authored: multiplication, fractions as numbers, area. Grades 4-5 have no questions yet.

requirements.title: Grades 6-8 cover ratios, algebra, geometry, statistics + full modular arithmetic, quadratics, graph theory, proof
requirements.notes: Map covers ratios, algebra, geometry, statistics plus modular arithmetic, quadratics, graph theory and proof for 6-8. Only g6-nscoord and g6-ratios authored.

requirements.title: Comic lessons with sequential panels and interactive elements
Practice problems: varied types, immediate feedback, hints, full solutions
requirements.notes: Five question types authored and graded server-side. Graph/plot input and dynamic geometry still missing.

requirements.title: Algorithmically generated problem variants
requirements.notes: Seeded templates for five topics give unlimited fresh variants. The seed travels in the question id, so the server can rebuild and mark the exact problem later without storing it — which also means a review item shows the identical question. Grading, hints and error analysis all work unchanged on generated questions.

requirements.title: Open-ended puzzles with multiple solution paths
requirements.notes: 8 open-ended puzzles across four difficulties, sitting outside the adaptive path. Hints come one at a time and a wrong answer never reveals the solution, which is what keeps a puzzle worth returning to. Multiple valid solution PATHS are encouraged by the prompts, but the checker accepts a final value rather than reasoning.

requirements.title: Proof exercises (drag-drop blocks, fill-in, free-form)
requirements.notes: Ordering, fill-in-the-reason and missing-step exercises implemented. Free-form proof entry is not built - it would need real symbolic or AI validation, and I will not claim structural checking is the same thing.

requirements.title: Explainer videos with captions and speed control
requirements.notes: Requires video production; no assets exist.

requirements.title: Interactive simulations and dynamic geometry
Assessments: diagnostic, formative, summative
requirements.notes: All three kinds reachable: adaptive diagnostic, formative practice with immediate feedback and explanation, and summative mastery check with a pass mark.

requirements.title: Text-to-speech read-aloud with text highlighting
requirements.notes: Read-aloud on every question using the browser's own speech synthesis, with maths spoken as words rather than symbols (times, divided by, half, quarter, the point 3 comma -2, the absolute value of -7). The control hides itself where speech is unsupported. Word-by-word text highlighting while reading is not implemented.

requirements.title: Productive struggle: attempts before hints; first hint never gives the solution
Mastery-based progression: 90% core, 80% advanced
requirements.notes: Server decides the threshold from the topic's track (core 90, adv 80) and returns it with each run; client no longer guesses.

requirements.title: Spaced review adapting to individual forgetting curves
requirements.notes: SM-2 style scheduler per (learner, topic): interval grows by an ease factor on success and collapses to one day on a lapse, with ease floored at 1.3. Every run, adaptive session and mastery check updates it.

requirements.title: Proof and justification progression K-8
requirements.notes: Progression exists: choosing a supporting reason at grade 1, ordering an argument at grade 3, two-column style with reasons at grade 5, contradiction at grade 6, induction at grade 8. Only five proofs authored so far.

requirements.title: Competition readiness: Contest Corner with past problems and drills
requirements.notes: Timed contest formats exist. No Contest Corner UI or strategy guides yet.

requirements.title: Number theory track
requirements.notes: Number theory topics mapped K-8 (k-evenodd through g8-rsa). No questions authored.

requirements.title: Combinatorics track
requirements.notes: Combinatorics topics mapped K-8 (k-combos through g8-designs). No questions authored.

requirements.title: Algebra extensions
requirements.notes: Algebra extension topics mapped G2-G8. No questions authored.

requirements.title: Geometry extensions
requirements.notes: Geometry extension topics mapped G2-G8. No questions authored.

requirements.title: Probability and statistics extensions
requirements.notes: Probability/statistics extension topics mapped G4-G8. No questions authored.

requirements.title: Proof techniques track
requirements.notes: Direct proof, proof by contradiction (infinitude of primes) and induction (sum formula) are represented. Pigeonhole and extremal principle are not.

requirements.title: Content authored/reviewed by educators with competition experience
requirements.notes: Process requirement about people, not code. Needs the user to define a review workflow and reviewers.

requirements.title: Reviewed for diversity, inclusivity, absence of stereotypes
WCAG 2.1 AA accessible content incl. alt text and captions
requirements.notes: UI meets WCAG 2.1 AA (check:accessibility-wcag-aa), images and SVGs carry text alternatives, and questions can be read aloud. Video captions and alt text for authored lesson art are not applicable yet - no such content exists.

requirements.title: Math notation via LaTeX with MathML accessibility
requirements.notes: Arithmetic, fractions, absolute value, coordinates, ratios and exponents render as MathML with an aria-label giving the spoken form, so assistive technology announces mathematics rather than punctuation. Negative numbers use a true minus sign. Unrecognised text is returned as escaped plain text rather than wrapped in markup that would misrepresent it. LaTeX input for authors is not supported - MathML was chosen because it needs no client library and is what assistive technology consumes.

requirements.title: Content versioned and approved through CMS workflow
Onboarding: grade selection or diagnostic assessment with skill map
requirements.notes: Adaptive diagnostic held server-side: difficulty steps up after two correct, down after two wrong. Produces a per-section skill map and a placement recommendation, stored against the learner and retrievable. Verified that strong and weak learners place differently.

requirements.title: Dashboard: dual-track map, avatar, daily goals, streaks, challenge of the day
requirements.notes: Grade/topic/tier navigation plus placement and mastery entry points. No avatar customisation, daily goals, streaks or challenge of the day.

requirements.title: Lesson player with comic panels, narration, embedded checks, resume
Practice mode: adaptive sequence, 3-level hints, feedback, stars, mistake review
requirements.notes: Adaptive session held server-side: difficulty follows performance, three-level hints reduce the star award, and every mistake is returned at the end with its answer and explanation. Time on task recorded.

requirements.title: Puzzle area with trophies and elegant-solution badges
requirements.notes: Puzzle area with untimed play, per-puzzle hints, gold/silver/bronze trophies reflecting how many hints were taken, and an Elegant Solution badge for solving unaided. Points scale with difficulty and are awarded once.

requirements.title: Mastery checks: no hints, configurable threshold, retake
requirements.notes: Server-issued check drawn across all tiers, marked server-side, hints refused with 409 while live, replay blocked, recorded under its own 'mastery' tier. Retake is allowed and counted.

requirements.title: Review and remediation driven by spaced repetition
requirements.notes: Review endpoint merges unmastered topics with those the spacing schedule says are due, each labelled with a reason. No dedicated review UI yet.

requirements.title: Social: moderated leaderboards, clans, no direct messaging
requirements.notes: Leaderboards are OFF by default and only a teacher can enable them, per class. Anonymised unless the teacher allows names, though a parent always sees their own child labelled. No global board and no messaging of any kind. Clans and team challenges are not built.

requirements.title: Competition prep mode: timed sets, mock contests, analytics
requirements.notes: Timed papers in five formats (Kangaroo, MOEMS, AMC 8, MATHCOUNTS, quick drill), scored server-side with the deadline owned by the server: a late submission is still marked but scores zero. Per-format history and topic breakdown recorded. NOT done: percentile ranking against other students, leaderboards, and a curated archive of real contest problems (licensing is blocked, 10.9).

requirements.title: Proof trainer with validation and template library
requirements.notes: Proof trainer with three exercise kinds (order the steps, match each step to its reason, supply the missing step) across grades 1 to 8. Checking is structural and honest about it: an ordering proof is right when the steps are in a valid order, a reasons proof when each step is paired with a justification that supports it. Feedback names which steps are wrong without revealing the answer. NOT done: free-form proof entry with validation, and the template library.

requirements.title: AI tutor: chat hints, misconception detection, safety filters
requirements.notes: Needs an LLM provider account, API key and a billing decision from the user.

requirements.title: Create and manage multiple child accounts
Set curriculum track per child (Core/Enrichment/Competition)
Progress monitoring: level, mastery, time spent, readiness
requirements.notes: Mastery, run history and per-session time on task recorded. No aggregate time-spent reporting or competition-readiness view.

requirements.title: Weekly email summary
requirements.notes: Needs an SMTP provider and credentials from the user.

requirements.title: Alerts when struggling, inactive, or ready to advance
requirements.notes: Error categories and the review queue give the raw signal for struggling. No alerting or notification yet (needs the blocked email/push provider).

requirements.title: Goal setting with notifications
requirements.notes: Parents set a weekly rounds target per learner; progress is computed from runs actually recorded in the last seven days, with met and at-risk flags. Notifications when a goal is met or at risk need the blocked email/push provider (9.4).

requirements.title: Curriculum overview with sample problems
Class management and rostering import
requirements.notes: Teachers hold a role; classes have join codes and the PARENT adds their own learner, so a teacher can never pull in a child unilaterally. LMS/rostering import (Clever, ClassLink, Google Classroom) is blocked on vendor accounts (9.1).

requirements.title: Assignment tools with due dates and per-group tracks
requirements.notes: Assignments per class with optional tier and due date, validated against real topics. Per-group differentiation and individual accommodations not built.

requirements.title: Class progress dashboard and standards heatmap
requirements.notes: Class dashboard shows every learner against every assignment with best score and mastery, plus a per-topic heatmap of attempts, average and mastery counts. Cross-teacher and parent access both refused.

requirements.title: Reporting: PDF/CSV export incl. gifted report
requirements.notes: Learner and class CSV exports plus a printable HTML report the browser turns into a PDF, which keeps a PDF engine out of the dependency tree. A dedicated gifted-and-talented report is not built.

requirements.title: Competition team management
School/district management
requirements.notes: Admin role granted out of band via ADMIN_EMAILS, never self-assignable at signup (verified). Platform-wide counts and role breakdown. Multi-school and multi-district hierarchy is not modelled.

requirements.title: Usage and performance analytics
requirements.notes: Aggregate analytics: user and learner counts, active learners in the last seven days, attainment distribution across four bands, and the ten hardest topics by average score. Verified to contain no learner name or parent email — administrators see shape, not individual children's work.

requirements.title: Compliance: retention policies and audit logs
requirements.notes: Retention policy published with live counts, audit log readable by admins, and admin access to the audit log is itself audited (verified). Automated deletion on a retention schedule is not built; erasure is self-service and immediate.

requirements.title: Points, with advanced content worth more
requirements.notes: Points awarded on every finished round, weighted higher for advanced topics as the spec requires, and reduced by hint use without ever going negative.

requirements.title: 100+ badges incl. subject and meta badges
requirements.notes: 12 badges across subject-specific, meta and puzzle achievements, awarded once and never revoked. The check now also scans the source for every badge the code can award and fails if any is missing from the catalogue - added after an uncatalogued badge shipped. The spec asks for 100+; this is a working subset.

requirements.title: Avatar customisation tied to achievements
Levels and prestige for advanced tracks
requirements.notes: Overall level derived from points on a square-root curve, with the next threshold reported. Per-subject levels and prestige for advanced tracks not built.

requirements.title: Streaks with freezes
requirements.notes: Daily streak counted from activity, breaking when a day is skipped, with 3-day and 7-day badges. Streak freezes not built.

requirements.title: Narrative arc with student-influenced outcomes
Unlockable content and hidden areas
Leaderboards, tournaments, clans
requirements.notes: Class leaderboards with teacher control and anonymisation. School-wide and global boards are deliberately not built - they would rank a child against strangers. Weekly tournaments and clan challenges are not implemented.

requirements.title: Mini-games reinforcing concepts
Achievement titles for advanced mastery
requirements.notes: Six titles earned by combinations of badges - Grand Combinatorialist, Master of Modular Arithmetic, Proof-Wright, Contest Contender, Steady Hand, Apprentice - ordered strongest first so the displayed title is the best held. Every title's requirements are validated against real badges.

requirements.title: Adaptive diagnostic using IRT/BKT producing a skill map
requirements.notes: Adaptive diagnostic with a skill map, and BKT now tracks per-skill knowledge (check:knowledge-tracing). Item Response Theory is still not implemented, and the diagnostic itself still uses the streak rule rather than the model.

requirements.title: Knowledge graph of prerequisite skills incl. advanced nodes
requirements.notes: 459 authored edges across 315 topics, acyclic, 239 of them crossing grades. Includes the dependencies the spec names (modular arithmetic requires division with remainders; combinatorics requires the multiplication principle). Exposed via /api/topics/:id/prereqs and a /next endpoint that separates what a learner is ready for from what is blocked, naming the missing prerequisites.

requirements.title: BKT/DKT mastery updates and bandit difficulty selection
requirements.notes: Bayesian Knowledge Tracing implemented and verified: P(known) updated per answer with slip and guess terms, guess rate scaled to the number of options, and mastery requiring both confidence and enough observations so a lucky answer cannot declare it. Estimates feed the readiness recommendation. NOT done: Deep Knowledge Tracing, per-skill parameter fitting from real data, and multi-armed bandit question selection - difficulty still steps by streak.

requirements.title: Spaced repetition scheduling with adaptive intervals
requirements.notes: Intervals adapt to the individual learner's performance rather than a fixed calendar. Review items are labelled with why they appear (not_yet_mastered or due_for_review). Interleaving review questions into live practice sets is not yet done.

requirements.title: Intervention triggers for struggle and rapid mastery
requirements.notes: Server-side triggers during a practice session: three consecutive wrong answers suggests reviewing or taking a hint; more than ten minutes on one question suggests a hint; a flawless unaided run at the hardest tier suggests moving to the advanced track. Decided server-side so the client cannot suppress them, and surfaced in the practice UI.

requirements.title: Multi-track adaptation with separate core/advanced models
requirements.notes: Core and advanced tracks carry separate mastery thresholds and BKT keeps a separate estimate per topic, so a learner can sit at different levels in different strands. Parent/teacher override of track assignment is not built.

requirements.title: Formative embedded questions with immediate feedback
Summative mastery checks and unit tests
requirements.notes: Chapter-level mastery checks implemented and verified. Unit tests across several topics, and AI-graded open-ended items, not built.

requirements.title: Feedback types incl. partial credit and elegance bonus
requirements.notes: Partial credit on multi-step answers: ordering earns credit for positions in the right place, select-all rewards correct picks and penalises wrong ones so guessing everything scores worse than a careful partial answer. Single-answer types stay all-or-nothing. An elegance bonus for creative solutions is not built - it would need judgement this cannot make honestly.

requirements.title: Three-level hints reducing star rating
Error analysis categorising common mistakes
requirements.notes: Wrong answers are classified into named misconceptions (sign error, reversed coordinates, place value, off by one, partial/over selection, reversed ordering, blank). Recorded per learner and reported by category and topic. Unrecognised mistakes are reported as unclassified rather than forced into a bucket.

requirements.title: Mastery thresholds configurable, default 90/80
requirements.notes: Defaults 90/80 enforced server-side and verified. Not yet configurable per teacher/admin, and mastery does not decay.

requirements.title: Web authoring tools for all content types
requirements.notes: Content is authored as reviewed source modules with a validating linter and CI enforcement rather than a web editor. A browser-based authoring tool with templates and versioning is not built.

requirements.title: Asset management with tagging and licensing
Curriculum mapping to standards
Localisation of text, audio and notation
QA workflow with preview and automated checks
requirements.notes: Content linter over every question, puzzle, proof and generator template: structural integrity, duplicates, explanations that merely restate the question, hints identical to the solution, options that give the answer away by length, and reading level against the grade. Each of the 13 rules is proven to fire on deliberately broken content, so a clean run means something. Preview-as-student and an approval workflow are not built.

requirements.title: Clever/ClassLink/Google Classroom rostering and SSO
requirements.notes: Each requires a vendor developer account and approval the user must obtain.

requirements.title: REST API, webhooks, GraphQL
requirements.notes: REST API exists. No webhooks or GraphQL.

requirements.title: Data export CSV/PDF and FERPA-compliant student export
requirements.notes: CSV for learners and classes, printable report, and the full JSON account export from /api/me/export. CSV escaping verified against a name containing a comma and quotes; access control verified on every export.

requirements.title: Email and push notifications
requirements.notes: Needs SMTP/push provider credentials.

requirements.title: LTI 1.3 Advantage support
Performance: lesson load < 2s broadband, < 5s 3G
requirements.notes: Server-side latency measured on every endpoint a screen needs, all well inside budget, plus payload size and concurrency checks including that 10 simultaneous writes all record without corrupting the progress row. This measures the SERVER only: real page-load time over broadband or 3G depends on network and device and cannot be established from here.

requirements.title: Scalability to 50,000 concurrent users
requirements.notes: SQLite single-node will not meet this; needs Postgres and horizontal scaling.

requirements.title: Security and privacy: COPPA, FERPA, GDPR, encryption, RBAC, audit logs
requirements.notes: Done and verified: security headers incl. CSP, brute-force limiting on login, COPPA consent required at registration, audit log, FERPA/GDPR export and erasure, secure cookie in production, and RBAC across parent, teacher and admin roles with admin not self-assignable. NOT done: encryption at rest (needs a deployment/KMS decision), automated retention deletion, and a third-party penetration test.

requirements.title: Reliability: 99.95% uptime, backups, offline degradation
requirements.notes: Consistent backups via VACUUM INTO, verified restorable and integrity-checked, now running on a schedule with bounded retention. Graceful shutdown drains in-flight requests. NOT done: uptime SLA, point-in-time recovery, multi-region failover, and a restore drill that rebuilds a running service from a snapshot.

requirements.title: Accessibility WCAG 2.1 AA incl. keyboard and screen reader
requirements.notes: axe-core over real rendered markup of 5 screens, zero WCAG 2.1 A/AA violations; 24 contrast pairs >= 4.5:1 in both themes; skip link, landmarks, live regions, non-colour correctness markers, labelled controls, visible focus.

requirements.title: Cross-platform web + native iOS/Android with offline sync
requirements.notes: Responsive web app with an offline shell, verified to build and emit every shell file. Native iOS and Android apps are not built, and offline PRACTICE (queuing answers while disconnected and syncing later) is not implemented - only the shell loads offline.

requirements.title: Usability: age-appropriate UI, onboarding, multilingual
Localisation incl. RTL
Legal compliance incl. content licensing
requirements.notes: Legal review and contest-problem licensing are the user's decisions.

requirements.title: Web client with PWA capability
requirements.notes: Installable PWA: manifest, maskable icon, theme colour, and a service worker caching the app shell for offline opening. The API is deliberately never cached - a cached answer could be replayed against the grader and stale progress would be worse than an honest offline message. Registered only in production builds.

requirements.title: API gateway and microservices
requirements.notes: Single Express service with modular routes; not decomposed.

requirements.title: Postgres + NoSQL + Redis + Elasticsearch
requirements.notes: Currently SQLite only, deliberately, to avoid external accounts.

requirements.title: CDN and video streaming
requirements.notes: Static assets are served by the API process with cache headers. No CDN - that is a deployment decision that follows from choosing a host.

requirements.title: Analytics pipeline and AI services
requirements.notes: Depends on the AI provider decision.

requirements.title: OAuth2/OIDC, rate limiting, DDoS protection, KMS
CI/CD with automated tests and IaC
requirements.notes: CI runs the full requirement suite on every push. A single-container Dockerfile builds the client and serves it from the API, with configs for Fly.io and Render pointing health checks at /ready and mounting persistent storage for SQLite. The check boots the production build and verifies it serves client, assets and API, that the SPA fallback does not swallow unknown API routes, and that Secure/HttpOnly cookies and HSTS are set. NOT done: an actual deployment (needs a host account), blue-green releases, and Infrastructure as Code.

requirements.title: All K-8 core and advanced curriculum loaded and standards-aligned
requirements.notes: 198 questions across 16 topics in 5 grades (K, 1, 2, 3, 6), every one validated: at least 5 questions and 2 tiers per topic, explanations present, options unique, ordering answers permutations of their items, and every authored topic on the prerequisite graph. 312 of 328 topics still have no content, and standards alignment tagging is not started.

requirements.title: Adaptive engine validated with 1,000 beta students per grade
requirements.notes: Requires real users; cannot be satisfied by code alone.

requirements.title: End-to-end flow: diagnostic to lesson to practice to mastery check to review
requirements.notes: Diagnostic -> practice -> review queue -> mastery check -> progress verified as one journey. The 'lesson' step of the spec's flow is not included: comic lessons (3.2.1) do not exist yet.

requirements.title: Competition mode and proof trainer operational
requirements.notes: Competition mode and proof trainer are both operational with sample content and verified end to end. Neither has the breadth of content the spec envisages.

requirements.title: AI tutor under 3s response with safety filters
Parent, teacher, admin dashboards showing accurate real-time data
requirements.notes: All three dashboards exist and are verified against real recorded work: parent progress, teacher class heatmap, and admin aggregate analytics. Each is access-controlled and shows only what that role should see.

requirements.title: Rostering and LTI integrations tested
WCAG 2.1 AA audit passes
requirements.notes: Automated AA audit passes on every screen built so far and runs in CI. A manual screen-reader pass (NVDA/VoiceOver) is still worth doing before release; automated tooling catches roughly half of WCAG issues.

requirements.title: Penetration testing shows no critical vulnerabilities
Load testing confirms 50,000 concurrent users
requirements.notes: Modest concurrency verified (40 simultaneous reads, 10 simultaneous writes, no corruption). The spec's 50,000 concurrent users needs a load-testing rig and horizontal scaling; SQLite on a single node will not meet it.

requirements.title: Mobile apps approved on both stores with offline mode
requirements.notes: Requires paid developer accounts the user must hold.

requirements.title: Mock contest scored accurately with correct leaderboards
requirements.notes: Mock contests score accurately and timing is enforced, both verified. Leaderboards are not built.

requirements.title: Proof checker accurate for sample proofs at each grade
requirements.notes: Structural checking is accurate for every authored proof at each grade level, verified for both acceptance and rejection. This is not a general proof checker.

requirements.title: Answers never sent to the client; server grades
requirements.notes: Not in the spec explicitly, but required by 4.1.4 hints and assessment integrity.

requirements.title: Passwords stored hashed; sessions in httpOnly cookies
Learner data isolated between accounts
Progress durable across restarts
Schema migrations apply to existing databases
requirements.notes: Found the hard way: CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS skips existing tables, so new columns never reached the dev database and every request 500'd. Migrations are now idempotent and a check boots against an old-schema file.

requirements.title: Account recoverable: password reset without data loss
requirements.notes: Reset tokens are stored only as a SHA-256 hash, single use, 30 minute expiry, and requesting one gives an identical response whether or not the account exists. Completing a reset revokes every existing session, so it locks out whoever prompted it. Learner and progress data survive intact. NOTE: with no email provider (9.4 blocked) the token is returned directly to the caller, which is rate limited but means anyone who can reach the endpoint for a known address can reset it. Set DELIVER_RESET_TOKEN=false once SMTP exists.

requirements.title: Graceful shutdown and error handling
requirements.notes: Express error handler returns JSON and never a stack trace; malformed and oversized bodies handled. SIGTERM drains in-flight requests and exits 0 within a 10s timeout, so a redeploy does not lose writes. uncaughtException logs and shuts down rather than serving from an unknown state.

requirements.title: Backups run on a schedule
requirements.notes: BACKUP_INTERVAL_HOURS runs backups on a timer with bounded retention, verified by running a server on a one-second interval and confirming snapshots appear, pruning holds, and the result passes an integrity check. Off by default so development does not litter the disk.
